mutant.description: One single-edit mutant on this worker's own artifact: test_ogv2_ac01's tool-set assertion (test_local_acceptance.py) widened from 'sorted(payload[...]) == sorted(de.SCHWAB_TOOLS)' to '... == sorted(de.SCHWAB_TOOLS) + ["MUTANT_EXTRA_TOOL"]', run, then reverted and its sha256 compared byte for byte. A second control on the independent-fixture instrument: OGV2-AC2's A8-refusals comparisons are, BY MEASUREMENT (not by injection), exactly the case where the app's real answer diverges from expect_independent.py's independent expectation -- proof the comparison is live, not vacuous, without needing a second injected mutant on code this worker cannot edit (query.py/integration.py are outside this order's <paths> grant).
mutant.expected: Mutated: test_ogv2_ac01 fails (AssertionError, right side carries one extra item). Restored: sha256 identical to pre-mutation; test_ogv2_ac01 passes again.
mutant.observed: Mutated: rc=1, 'AssertionError: assert [...] == [...]; Right contains one more item: 'MUTANT_EXTRA_TOOL''. Restored: sha256 75ce95163b592c42f3bc326be11eb1fbd0efc907764ad13590a5f83611fcb1e5 before and after (identical); test_ogv2_ac01 back to '1 passed in 2.38s'. The independent-fixture control: OGV2-AC2's own run shows the comparison catching a real divergence (A8-refusals) while the other four comparison groups in the same test (balance totals, position groups, market-value totals, date deltas) match exactly -- so the harness discriminates, it does not always agree.
